stem: Why should a technician avoid assigning developmental stage from days since a photoperiod change alone?
choices: A standardized production calendar is more objective than morphology, but only after the first week
Observable development can vary with genotype, plant history and environment, so calendar timing is context rather than proof of biological stage
Calendar stage should override outlier morphology so all plants in one room keep the same record label
Morphology is useful only after mature inflorescences are visible, so earlier stage labels must come from the schedule
rationale: Schedule timing can be useful context, but peer-reviewed life-cycle observations show that developmental descriptions are supported by visible morphology and study-specific timing should not be treated as universal across crops.
